channel.title: Said & Checked: Civil Rights and Social Issues — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Civil Rights and Social Issues, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Civil Rights and Social Issues, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 6 unsettled (Melanie Stansbury, Jamie Raskin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Melanie Stansbury, U.S. Representative from New Mexico: “This bill would undermine the fundamentals of Tribal sovereignty and the ability of our Tribal nations to protect cultural and sacred sites” Unsettled. The introduced text removes National Historic Preservation Act section 306108 consultation for reissued general permits and some covered activities, and limits NEPA suits over actions on tribal trust resources. It also lets tribes grant rights-of-way without Interior approval of each grant, adds a path to Clean Water Act Section 401 authority and funds Tribal Historic Preservation Officers. The net effect on tribal sovereignty turns on legal reading.
  • Melanie Stansbury, U.S. Representative from New Mexico: “In contrast to how the current administration is attempting to plaster Washington, D.C., with vanity projects requested by the President in violation of current law” Unsettled. Judge Leon and a D.C. Circuit panel found the White House ballroom likely unlawful without congressional authorization. The Supreme Court stayed that injunction 5-4 on standing grounds without deciding legality, and a certiorari petition is pending. Suits over the planned arch are undecided. No final ruling or GAO finding was found. Court holdings are as reported by NPR and SCOTUSblog.
  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative from Maryland: “It spread across the Colonies and became the best-selling book of all time, other than the Bible, in the Colonies.” Unsettled. Sources describe Common Sense as a sensation (the Thomas Paine Society cites over 500,000 copies) but note that historians dispute the copy counts, and none ranks it against the Bible.

13 statements by 5 officeholders. 12 checked: 6 supported, 6 unsettled · 1 not checkable.

item.title: Said & Checked, Civil Rights and Social Issues, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Ron DeSantis, Mike Pence)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Ron DeSantis, Governor of Florida: “What they are doing is not mandated by Florida law” Unsettled. This turns on how the statute is read. Florida's SB 1134, effective Jan. 1, 2027, bars a municipality from funding or promoting activities designed with reference to ethnicity, among other categories, and exempts content-neutral event permits and recognition of state and federal holidays. It names no parades and requires no cancellation.
  • Mike Pence, Former Vice President of the United States: “this is an administration that literally has not lifted a finger to support states that are trying to stem the flow of mail-order abortion pills around the country.” Unsettled. The FDA's own page says mifepristone "may be dispensed in person or by mail", with no restriction added, and KFF reports the administration defended the FDA's rules in court in 2026 while citing an internal safety review. No federal action restricting mail-order pills was found, which fits the statement; the safety review is open, and "not lifted a finger" is loose wording the record cannot settle.

3 statements by 2 officeholders. 2 checked: 2 unsettled · 1 not checkable.
